messages:
suresh: Heads-up — mid-day traffic burst caused p99 to climb from ~700ms to ~2.8s for about 7m. I pulled a quick profile, looks like a lot of requests hit a kernel fallback + KV cold reads during scale-up. attaching snippets below.

marta: Ugh. Do we have a single noisy model or was this across variants?

suresh: Mostly v1.2 and the LLM-quant variants. Kernel selector shows ~38% of requests fell back to the conservative kernel at sequence lengths >768. Also microbatch size skewed low (3-6 reqs) during the burst.

kevin: ops-bot alert?

ops-bot: incident_alert: p99_latency=2803ms, p95_latency=940ms, error_rate=0.2% for route /v1/generate over window 11:32–11:39 UTC. Autoscaler triggered +2 nodes at 11:34 but new nodes became healthy at 11:36.

elia: Can you paste the profiler command you used? Want to correlate with kernel traces.

suresh: Ran the per-shard flame + kernel-selector trace:
```
runtime-profiler --host shard-12 --since 11:30 --until 11:40 --focus=kernel,kv_cache,queue
```
Snippet from trace: 
````
kernel_choice: fast-kernel 60% -> fallback small-kernel 40%
avg_batch_size: 4.1 (target ideal 8-12)
kv_cache_miss: 0.18 per request on avg (spike to 0.62 at 11:34)
queue_wait_ms: median 12ms, p99 520ms during 11:33–11:36
```

hana: So two signals: low microbatching (bad throughput) + KV cold misses during scale-up. Which one is the dominant tail driver?

suresh: I ran an isolated offline replay with two toggles: forced kv-warmup and forced batch-doubling. Results:
- kv-warmup only -> p99 from 2.8s -> 1.1s
- batch doubling only (increase microbatch target from 8->16) -> p99 from 2.8s -> 1.5s
- both -> p99 ~900ms.

remy: Interesting, so KV warming buys more tail reduction than batching in this case. Any regression in kernel selector logic recently?

suresh: We merged a kernel-threshold tweak two days ago that tightens the condition for the fast kernel when avg seq len variance > 0.2. It looks like with the burst the variance jumped, so selector opted for conservative kernel more often. That increased per-token latency and reduced ability to pack microbatches.

marta: Could autoscaler policy be adjusted to pre-warm nodes earlier for known scheduled bursts? Or temporary burst-capacity reservation?

kevin: Two options: 1) reduce kernel selector sensitivity during short bursts (less likely to fallback), 2) pre-warm KV cache on newly provisioned nodes (background warmup of top prefixes), 3) tweak autoscaler to scale earlier based on prober signal.

elia: For 1) we should be cautious — fast kernel on mismatched profiles can regress throughput in other cases. Propose an A/B: on a small % of traffic, relax selector during autoscale events and measure tail.

hana: For 2) how heavy is warmup? Do we have a cheap prefix set to ping?

suresh: Warmup baseline: hitting top 500 prefixes over a 60s window reduced kv_miss to ~0.02. Cost of warmup ~0.3 tokens per second per node (very small).

remy: Nice. For autoscaler tuning: the current prober samples 10 reqs/sec per shard. During the burst that was too sparse to detect. Increase prober to 50 reqs/sec for first 2 minutes after any traffic ramp, then decay.

ops-bot: deploy-check requested by elia: canary plan for kernel-sensitivity rollback + kv-warmup enabled for canary shards.

marta: Action items:
- elia: implement canary flow for selector relax + add metric `selector_fallback_rate` (due EOD)
- kevin: ops: prototype KV warmup script + integrate into node init (due tomorrow)
